title: No rule holds a commit body to the 72-column wrap that every CONTRIBUTING.md states
foundBy: user report (host): "Commit bodies with longer lines than what's recommended in our various contributing.md ... this as well should be a warning if it's already pushed and an error on new commits"

evidence.verified: `go test ./internal/oss/ -run 'Wrap|TrailerBlock|NoBodySkips' -count=1` passes 4 tests. A line of 73 columns is one error before a push and one warning after it. A line of 72 columns passes, and so does one of 72 characters that takes 96 bytes. A long Co-Authored-By trailer passes, while a trailer-shaped line followed by prose and a lower-case key each give one error. Against the code at 0e71b10, all four tests fail with `no rule OSS-713`. Four changes to the code each fail one of them: counting bytes, dropping the trailer exemption, taking lower-case keys as trailers, and finding a trailer anywhere. The binary built at 6b49610 warns on 4 bodies in lint, 1 in ledger, 23 in tracer and 6 in vcr. It warns on 19 in sandbox, 31 in campaign and 29 in ui. A separate count of the same histories agrees. In ui all 29 predate the baseline of `scripts/check-commits.mjs`, which reports 184 commits since it, all wrapped. `make ci` passed at 6b49610.

resolution: OSS-713 measures each commit body in characters and reports a line wider than 72. The trailer block at the foot of the message is exempt and nothing else is, as in the script ui kept for this. A body no remote carries fails the run, and one a remote carries prints as a warning and passes.
details:
Every sibling project's `CONTRIBUTING.md` says to wrap a commit body at 72 columns, and `cs-lint oss` checks every other part of that section. The wrap is the gap. ui fills it with a script of its own, `scripts/check-commits.mjs`, whose header names an OSS rule in cs-lint as its durable home. The other projects have nothing.

Bodies with a line past 72 columns are common. At the time of filing there are 4 in lint, 1 in ledger, 23 in tracer and 6 in vcr. There are 19 in sandbox, 31 in campaign and 29 in ui. The widest runs to 314 columns, a whole paragraph on one line. A body is free to rewrap before it is pushed and costs a rewrite after. So the finding should be an error on a new commit and a warning on one a remote already carries.
